scope: KNDS group product portfolio, part A (Teilauftrag A): current public status (announcement, prototype/testing, series production/deliveries, operational use by customers) for LEOPARD 2 A7 / A7V / A8, LECLERC XLR, PUMA, BOXER RCT30, GRIFFON, JAGUAR, SERVAL, VBCI, FENNEK, DINGO, MUNGO and GFF4. Facts only; no stage assignment. Statements in English.

claims.statement: KNDS describes the LEOPARD 2 A7/A7V as a main battle tank developed and qualified for the Bundeswehr with 120-mm armament; the A7 is described as existing Bundeswehr equipment.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: A7 developed and qualified for the Bundeswehr; the Bundeswehr has it; 120-mm smoothbore gun.
claims.uncertainty: The product page mixes A7 and A7V; no extrapolation to A8.

claims.statement: According to KNDS, the Leopard 2 family is used by the armed forces of 22 nations, all vehicles were supplied by KNDS, and more than 3,500 units have been delivered; reference customers named include Germany, Switzerland, Spain, Denmark and Sweden.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: The LEOPARD 2 A7 product page states that the armed forces of 22 nations rely on the LEOPARD 2, that all vehicles were supplied by KNDS, 'over 3,500 units', with reference customers Germany, Switzerland, Spain, Denmark, Sweden 'and many more'.
claims.location: Section 'Cutting-edge battle tanks for the most demanding of missions' and 'Facts about the LEOPARD 2 A7V'
claims.uncertainty: Family-level figure for all Leopard 2 versions, not specific to the A7 version; no per-version user list on the page.

claims.statement: According to KNDS, it handed over the last of 44 Leopard 2A7HU main battle tanks to Hungary on 12 December 2025; KNDS states that delivery of all vehicle systems under the December 2018 contract was completed on schedule.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: Press release dated Munich, December 12, 2025: Hungarian army celebrates completion of the Leopard 2A7HU delivery with a parade; 'delivery of all vehicle systems has therefore been completed on schedule' under the contract signed in December 2018.
claims.uncertainty: The release concerns the Hungarian export configuration 2A7HU.

claims.statement: European Security & Defence reported that, according to the Hungarian Defence Minister, the first Leopard 2A7+HU tanks were handed over to Hungarian Army units (11th Armoured Battalion, Tata) in mid-December 2023, after first delivery to the Hungarian authorities in August 2023.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: ESD, 12 Jan 2024: tanks handed over to units in mid-December 2023 as announced by Defence Minister Szalay-Bobrovniczky on X; eight tanks delivered by 11 January 2024; remaining 36 due by 2025.
claims.uncertainty: Reporting relays the minister's announcement; later completion is covered by the KNDS release of 12 Dec 2025.

claims.statement: The Danish Armed Forces announced on 21 September 2023 that they had received the last of 44 Leopard 2 tanks upgraded from A5 to A7 standard at KMW (KNDS) facilities; the first two were delivered in 2019.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: Defence Industry Europe reports the Danish announcement of the last of 44 Leopard 2 tanks upgraded from the A5 to the A7 standard, handed over on 21 September at Holstebro; the first two A7 were delivered by KMW in 2019.
claims.uncertainty: Danish vehicles are upgraded existing tanks (Leopard 2A7 DK), not new builds.

claims.statement: KNDS describes the LEOPARD 2 A7V as developed and qualified for the new tasks of the German Bundeswehr and states that the Bundeswehr currently has one of the world's most modern main battle tanks; the A7V is listed with 120 mm L55/L55A1 smooth-bore armament.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The LEOPARD 2 A7V was developed and qualified for the new tasks of the German Bundeswehr'; specification table lists 120mm / L55 or L55A1 smooth-bore cannon.
claims.location: Sections 'Performance characteristics of the LEOPARD 2 A7V' and 'PRODUCT features – Specifications'
claims.uncertainty: The page states the Bundeswehr has the vehicle but gives no quantities or dates.

claims.statement: Defence Industry Europe reported that KMW delivered the final (104th) Leopard 2 tank modernised to the 2A7V standard to the Bundeswehr; the upgrade contract dated from 2017 (EUR 760 million) and deliveries had begun in 2019.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'KMW has delivered the final (104th) Leopard 2 tank modernized to the 2A7V standard to the Bundeswehr'; contract initiated 2017, EUR 760 million; deliveries of new tanks began in 2019.
claims.uncertainty: Trade-press report; the exact handover date is not stated in the text read (article published October 2023).

claims.statement: KMW stated at the first handover in October 2019 that Germany would receive 104 Leopard 2 A7V vehicles by 2023 and that Denmark would receive 44 Leopard 2 A7 vehicles by 2022.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: KMW handed the symbolic keys of the first two vehicles to the Danish ambassador and the Parliamentary State Secretary; 'The German Federal Armed Forces will gain 104 Leopard 2 A7V vehicles by 2023.'
claims.uncertainty: Plan statement from 2019; actual completion is covered by the Defence Industry Europe report of 2023.

claims.statement: Defence24 reported that a second modernisation contract of 101 Leopard 2 A6-family tanks to the 2A7V standard was signed in March 2019 (more than EUR 300 million), with the last vehicle due to be delivered in 2026.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'In March this year a contract for modernising a further batch – 101 vehicles – was signed, the last of which is to be delivered in 2026'; cost over EUR 300 million.
claims.uncertainty: Plan from a 2019 article; completion of this batch was not confirmed in sources read.

claims.statement: Janes reported that the first Leopard 2 equipped with the Trophy active protection system, a Leopard 2A7A1, was rolled out on 29 October 2024 and was to be delivered to the German Army in mid-2025, followed by 16 more by the end of 2025; it was undergoing testing by industry and WTD 41.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: Janes, 5 Dec 2024: first Trophy-equipped Leopard 2 (2A7A1 version) rolled out on 29 October; delivery to the German Army planned for mid-2025, then 16 more by end of 2025; testing by industry and WTD 41.
claims.uncertainty: Variant-specific (A7A1); the delivery dates are planned figures from December 2024 and are not confirmed in sources read.

claims.statement: According to KNDS, the Leopard 2A8 for the German and Norwegian armed forces was rolled out in Munich on 19 November 2025, with the German Defence Minister present; KNDS states that all Leopard 2A8 for the Bundeswehr are manufactured at its Munich site.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: Press release Munich, 19 November 2025: rollout of the KNDS LEOPARD 2A8 and PzH 2000 systems; 'All LEOPARD 2 A8 tanks for the Bundeswehr will be manufactured at the KNDS site in Munich.'
claims.uncertainty: Roll-out is a public presentation of the first vehicles, not a delivery.

claims.statement: According to KNDS, 123 Leopard 2 A8 are under contract for the Bundeswehr (contract signed in 2023) and 54 for the Norwegian Army; KNDS stated that handover to the soldiers of both nations would begin in April 2026 as contractually agreed.
claims.evidence: Excerpt: 'The handover of the LEOPARD 2 A8 main battle tanks to the soldiers of both nations will begin in April 2026, as contractually agreed.'; procurement of 123 LEOPARD 2 A8 (contract signed in 2023); 54 Norwegian tanks under contract.
claims.uncertainty: The April 2026 date is a stated contractual plan from Nov 2025; a first handover to the Bundeswehr was not found in sources read (see P-SA entries on Norway and Germany).

claims.statement: According to KNDS, the first two Leopard 2 A8 NO were delivered to the Norwegian Army on 30 April 2026; 17 of the 54 Norwegian tanks are manufactured by KNDS in Germany and 37 at a new production facility in Levanger, Norway, where production is scheduled to begin in autumn 2026 (capacity up to 36 tanks per year).
claims.evidence: Paraphrase (both sources): first Leopard 2A8 NO delivered to Norway on 30 April 2026; Levanger production start scheduled for autumn / Q3 2026.

evidence_items.text: Press release Munich/Levanger, April 29/30, 2026: 'on April 30, 2026, the first two Leopard 2 A8 NO were delivered to the Norwegian Army'; 17 of 54 manufactured by KNDS; 37 in Levanger; production scheduled to begin in autumn 2026; capacity up to 36 tanks per year.
Janes, 12 May 2026, reporting the KNDS release of 4 May 2026: first two Leopard 2A8NO delivered on 30 April; seventeen produced in Munich and 37 in Norway; production scheduled for Q3 2026.

claims.uncertainty: Delivery shows first series-built vehicles handed over; Levanger production start is future-dated in the sources; one outlet claims a production start on 15 Oct 2026 which was not confirmed by a second source and is not used.

claims.statement: Janes reported that planning calls for the Leopard 2A8NO to enter Norwegian Army service starting in 2027 after testing and verification, to be completed in 2028, replacing Leopard 2A4.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'Planning calls for the tanks to enter Norwegian Army service starting in 2027 after testing and verification and to be completed by 2028, replacing 30-year-old Leopard 2A4s.'
claims.uncertainty: Planning statement; operational use by a customer is not yet reported in the sources read.

claims.statement: A BAAINBw spokesperson told dpa in November 2025 that the first Leopard 2 A8 are to be delivered to the troops in 2027, with all 123 delivered by 2030; dpa added that the Bundeswehr is to receive initial vehicles for testing in 2026 and that the first battalions are to be equipped starting with the German troops assigned to Lithuania.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase (both sources): German troop deliveries from 2027 to 2030; test vehicles in 2026.

evidence_items.text: dpa via Yahoo News, 19 Nov 2025: BAAINBw spokesman: 'The first tanks are to be delivered to the troops in 2027, with the aim of having delivered all 123 main battle tanks to the troops by 2030'; Bundeswehr set to receive initial vehicles for testing in 2026.

Defense News, 20 Nov 2025: German army slated to get 123, 'with deliveries beginning in 2027 and to be finalized in 2030'; first batch for the Bundeswehr formation in Lithuania, which is to reach full operational status in 2027.

claims.uncertainty: The KNDS release of Nov 2025 names April 2026 as handover start for 'the soldiers of both nations'; the BAAINBw statement names 2027 for troops. The two statements are not reconciled and no first Bundeswehr handover was found by 29 Oct 2026.

claims.statement: hartpunkt reported in December 2025 that 301 Leopard 2 A8 were under contract: 123 for the Bundeswehr, 44 for Lithuania, 46 for the Netherlands, 44 for the Czech Republic and 44 for Croatia (the Croatian order placed by BAAINBw in December 2025), with options for at least 20 more.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'Insgesamt sind somit bis heute 301 Leopard 2 A8 unter Vertrag, davon 123 für die Bundeswehr, 44 für Litauen, 46 für die Niederlande, 44 für Tschechien und 44 für Kroatien.'
claims.uncertainty: Count excludes the 54 Norwegian tanks, which are under a separate contract; order is not delivery.

claims.statement: According to KNDS, the LECLERC main battle tank is being modernised under the SCORPION programme; the modernised version is called LECLERC XLR.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: Modernisation under the SCORPION programme; designated XLR after modernisation.
claims.uncertainty: No specific delivery date for XLR was inferred from the product description.

claims.statement: Europe 1, citing Nexter, reported in January 2023 that a first prototype Leclerc XLR tank had been handed to the DGA at the end of 2022 and that the first 18 series vehicles were to be delivered to the French Army in 2023.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'Les 18 premiers exemplaires de série doivent être livrés cette année à l'armée de Terre, un premier char prototype ayant été remis à la DGA fin 2022, selon Nexter.' (also: 50 further renovated Leclerc ordered, notified 29 December).
claims.uncertainty: The 2023 delivery figure is a plan; actual deliveries are covered by later claims.

claims.statement: Defence Redefined reported on 1 December 2023 that the French Army received its first modernised Leclerc XLR, delivered to the 501st Tank Regiment (501e RCC) at Mourmelon-le-Grand; 200 vehicles are scheduled for modernisation with completion planned for 2029.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The French Army (Armée de terre) received the first modernized Leclerc main battle tank (XLR version)... delivered to the 501st Armored Regiment'.
claims.uncertainty: The 2029 completion date is superseded by later LPM targets (160 by 2030, 40 more by 2035).

claims.statement: Defense Mirror reported that the 34th renovated Leclerc XLR tank was delivered to the French Army on 10 December 2024, that the DGA ordered 100 further renovations bringing the total ordered to 200 (previous orders in 2021 and 2022 of 50 each), and that work is carried out by KNDS France in Roanne.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase (both sources): 100 further XLR ordered 24 Dec 2024, total 200, work in Roanne; 34th delivery on 10 Dec 2024 (Defense Mirror).

evidence_items.text: Defense Mirror: 'The 34th renovated XLR tank was delivered to the French Army on December 10, 2024'; order for 100 more brings total to 200; work at KNDS France site in Roanne.
Defence Industry Europe, 29 Jan 2025: contract of 24 December 2024 for 100 additional Leclerc XLR, total ordered 200 after 50 in 2021 and 50 in 2022; work at KNDS France's Roanne facility.

claims.uncertainty: The count of 34 is reported only by Defense Mirror among sources read; no 2025/2026 delivery total was found.

claims.statement: According to the LPM 2024-2030 as reported by Defence Industry Europe, France plans to have 160 upgraded Leclerc XLR in service by the end of 2030 and 40 more modernised by 2035; new digital sights are planned from 2028.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'France plans to have 160 upgraded Leclerc XLR tanks in service by the end of 2030. An additional 40 will be modernised by 2035'; new digital sighting systems from 2028.
claims.uncertainty: Planning target, not delivery.

claims.statement: Defense Magazine reported in April 2025, citing the French Army, that a first Combined Arms Tactical Group (GTIA) could be equipped with 51 Leclerc XLR by the end of 2025, and that the XLR tanks being delivered by KNDS France do not yet have the planned PASEO sights.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'According to the French Army, it will be possible to equip a first GTIA with 51 Leclerc tanks upgraded to the XLR standard by the end of this year'; tanks delivered lack PASEO sights, ordered from Safran in February 2024.
claims.uncertainty: Plan statement for end 2025; actual end-2025 or 2026 totals were not found.

claims.statement: The French Army presented a Leclerc XLR with a roof-mounted anti-drone cage at Eurosatory on 14 June 2026; the head of the Army Technical Section stated that the cage is manufactured by KNDS France and is being delivered to the tank units, and that the Leclerc is being upgraded under SCORPION.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: Defense News, 15 Jun 2026: 'now being manufactured by KNDS France and in the process of being delivered to the tank units' (Gen. Olivier Coquet); upgraded Leclerc XLR shown at Eurosatory on 14 June 2026.
claims.uncertainty: Shows XLR tanks in army tank units; no XLR fleet count given.

claims.statement: The French Army's equipment page describes the Leclerc XLR as the renovated main battle tank of the French Army with a 120 mm gun, SCORPION vetronics, SICS and CONTACT radio, built by Nexter Systems.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: Ministère des Armées/Armée de Terre page 'Le char Leclerc XLR rénové': first fourth-generation battle tank, 120 mm gun, common SCORPION vetronics, SICS and radio CONTACT; constructor Nexter System.
claims.uncertainty: Undated reference page; shows official designation as army equipment, not delivery numbers.
claims.depth_reason: Identity/catalogue statement; status dated by other claims.

claims.statement: KNDS describes PUMA as an infantry fighting vehicle developed and manufactured jointly with Rheinmetall under PSM, with a 30-mm gun and remotely operated turret.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: PUMA development and manufacturing under PSM; 30-mm automatic cannon and unmanned turret.
claims.location: Cutting-edge technologies combined; Product features / Equipment features

claims.statement: The Bundeswehr states that the Puma has been introduced to the troops since 2015 and that its latest design standard S1 was under tactical and technical-logistical study at Regen and Pfreimd in July 2024, with the aim of bringing the S1 standard to operational readiness.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: Bundeswehr article 24.07.2024: 'Seit seiner Einführung 2015 in die Truppe wurde der Schützenpanzer stetig verbessert. Nun steht ... die neueste Variante mit dem Kürzel S1 auf dem taktischen Prüfstand'; 14-day examination.
claims.uncertainty: The study concerns the S1 design standard; it does not give fleet counts.

claims.statement: The Bundeswehr reported in June 2023 that an infantry company of Panzergrenadierbataillon 33 trained at Munster with 18 Puma infantry fighting vehicles and described the Puma as an established mainstay of the Army's heavy forces.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: Bundeswehr article 15.06.2023: Major Stephan O. commands 18 Schützenpanzer Puma and five Leopard 2 A6 during the exercise at the Schießübungszentrum Panzertruppen, Munster; Puma 'eine nicht mehr wegzudenkende Stütze für die Schweren Kräfte des Heeres'.
claims.uncertainty: One exercise report; not a fleet count.

claims.statement: hartpunkt reported that by the end of 2025 the German armed forces had procured 350 Puma of the first lot (337 infantry fighting vehicles and 13 driver-training vehicles), which are being brought to the S1 standard by industry, plus 50 Puma of the second lot in the S1 standard; the order for 200 more Puma S1 placed at the end of 2025 is to be delivered from 2028.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'Bis Ende 2025 haben die deutschen Streitkräfte insgesamt 350 Schützenpanzer-Puma (337 Schützenpanzer und 13 Fahrschulpanzer) des ersten Loses ... sowie 50 Schützenpanzer-Puma des zweiten Loses (Rüststand S1) beschafft.' Deliveries of the 200 start in 2028.
claims.uncertainty: Procured (ordered/acquired) counts, not a delivery ledger for the second lot.

claims.statement: Rheinmetall states that on 19 December 2025 BAAINBw signed an amendment to the PUMA framework contract with PSM, the Rheinmetall–KNDS joint venture, for 200 further Puma worth about EUR 4.2 billion gross (effective January 2026), and that the S1 retrofit of 297 Puma ordered in 2023 and 2024 will be completed in 2029; a further S2 amendment is planned for 2026.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: Rheinmetall press release: order of 200 Schützenpanzer Puma, EUR 4.2 billion gross, contract effective January 2026; S1 modernisation of 297 Puma 'wird 2029 abgeschlossen sein'; an amendment for design standard S2 'für 2026 geplant'.
claims.uncertainty: Order, retrofit target and planned amendment; none is a delivery.

claims.statement: According to PSM, the Rheinmetall–KNDS Puma joint venture, the first two systems from the second Puma lot were accepted by the public customer on 27 August and 3 September 2026 and the first system from the second lot in S1 configuration was handed over to the Bundeswehr on 28 August 2026; the first two systems undergo further testing at WTD 81 and WTD 91.
claims.evidence: Excerpt/paraphrase (see evidence_items): first Lot 2 delivery 28 Aug 2026.

evidence_items.text: 'Am 27.08. und 03.09.2026 wurden die ersten beiden Systeme durch den öffentlichen Auftraggeber erfolgreich abgenommen. Am 28.08.26 wurde das 1. System aus dem 2. Los im K-Stand S1 an die Bundeswehr erfolgreich übergeben.'
evidence_items.location: News item 'Erste Auslieferung aus dem 2. Los SPz PUMA', paragraphs 2-4

evidence_items.text: Militarnyi, Sept 2026: the first Puma of the second batch in S1 configuration was delivered to the Bundeswehr on 28 August 2026; first two vehicles accepted on 27 August and 3 September and sent to WTD 81 and WTD 91 for testing.

claims.uncertainty: Only the first system is reported delivered; the delivery rate for the remaining 49 Lot 2 vehicles is not published in sources read. Media coverage rests on the PSM statement.

claims.statement: According to KNDS, the BOXER RCT30 combines a modular 8x8 platform with a remotely operated 30-mm turret; interchangeable mission modules are part of the BOXER concept.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: BOXER modularity and PUMA firepower; remotely operated 30-mm turret.
claims.uncertainty: No delivery status established from the product entry alone.

claims.statement: According to KNDS, on 7 August 2026 OCCAR placed an order with ARTEC (joint venture of KNDS Deutschland and Rheinmetall) for 69 additional BOXER RCT30 by exercising an option under the 2025 contract for 222 systems: 35 additional vehicles for the Bundeswehr (total 185) and 34 for the Royal Netherlands Army (total 106).
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: Press release Munich, 7 August 2026: option under the contract concluded in 2025 for 222 systems exercised; 'The German Armed Forces ... will now receive an additional 35 vehicles'; the Netherlands will have a total of 106.
claims.uncertainty: Order only; no delivery claim. The release's Bundeswehr total is derived: 150 ordered earlier plus 35.

claims.statement: According to KNDS, KNDS Deutschland was subcontracted by ARTEC on 13 October 2025 to supply BOXER RCT 30 vehicles for the German Army (150 systems, fielded as 'Schakal') and 72 for the Dutch armed forces; KNDS states the first RCT 30 will be delivered starting in late 2027.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: Press release Munich, 13 October 2025 (as published by EDR): ARTEC contract with OCCAR; 150 Schakal for the Bundeswehr, 72 for the Netherlands; 'The first RCT 30 wheeled infantry fighting vehicles will be delivered starting in late 2027.'
claims.uncertainty: Deliveries are future-dated in the source; the release also notes the BOXER base is deployed in seven nations, which does not apply to the RCT30 configuration.

claims.statement: In its Eurosatory 2022 press release, KMW (now KNDS) described a BOXER infantry fighting vehicle (IFV) mission module with a crewless, remotely controllable turret and an airburst-capable 30 mm automatic gun, stating that the turret construction is familiar from the PUMA.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: Press release 'EUROSATORY 2022: KMW presents a world debut': 'The mission module of the IFV variant features a fully stabilised, crewless, remotely controllable turret ... The airburst-capable, fully stabilised, automatic 30 mm machine gun ... The familiar turret construction from the PUMA'.
claims.location: Paragraph describing the IFV variant mission module
claims.uncertainty: The release does not say that a functional IFV-variant vehicle was shown or tested; it is a description of the mission module. No test or qualification is reported.
claims.depth_reason: Description only; not evidence of a prototype or tests.

claims.statement: cpm Defence Network reported in June 2024, ahead of Eurosatory, that the Bundeswehr had decided in favour of the Boxer RCT30 for 150 wheeled infantry fighting vehicles and stated that the airburst-capable 30 mm gun's ability to engage targets accurately on the move 'was already demonstrated in tests'.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'die Entscheidung für den Boxer RCT30 – auch PuBo genannt – gefallen'; 'Dies wurde bereits in Tests nachgewiesen' (referring to the Puma-type turret's firing on the move).
claims.uncertainty: The test statement is not dated and refers to the turret/cannon; it does not identify a Boxer RCT30 prototype test campaign. Not used as prototype evidence.
claims.depth_reason: Selection decision reported by trade press; test reference is generic.

claims.statement: produktion.de reported in November 2025 that 222 Boxer RCT 30 are covered by the international procurement (150 for the Bundeswehr as 'Schakal', 72 for the Netherlands) and that delivery of the first systems is expected from the end of 2027.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'Insgesamt sind 222 Boxer RCT 30 Radschützenpanzer Teil dieses internationalen Beschaffungsvorhabens ... Die Auslieferung der ersten Systeme wird ab Ende 2027 erwartet.'
claims.location: Section 'Was steckt hinter der Beschaffung des Schakal?'
claims.uncertainty: Second-source confirmation of the stated delivery start; planned date.

claims.statement: militaeraktuell.at reported on 13 August 2026 that the exercised option raises the number of ordered vehicles to 291 in total and that the Bundeswehr introduces the Boxer RCT 30 as 'Schakal', combining the Boxer 8x8 drive module with the unmanned RCT-30 turret also used on Puma.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: option from the 2025 contract for 222 systems; the Bundeswehr introduces the Boxer RCT 30 under the name Schakal; combination of 8x8 drive module and unmanned RCT-30 turret.
claims.uncertainty: Second-source confirmation of the option; no delivery information in the text read.

claims.statement: KNDS France cites the production of GRIFFON and JAGUAR as well as SERVAL under the French SCORPION programme; the portfolio also includes VBCI.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: SCORPION production of GRIFFON/JAGUAR and SERVAL; VBCI in the KNDS France portfolio.
claims.uncertainty: Variants and current quantities are not determined from this overview.

claims.statement: KNDS describes the GRIFFON as a 6x6 armoured personnel carrier developed by the French consortium of KNDS France, Arquus and Thales and as a key component of the French Army's SCORPION programme, with eleven further versions including a 120 mm self-propelled mortar (MEPAC).
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The GRIFFON is a 6x6 armored vehicle developed by the French industrial consortium composed of KNDS France, Arquus, and Thales. It is a key component of the French Army's SCORPION modernization program.'
claims.uncertainty: Product description only; the page gives no delivery numbers.
claims.depth_reason: Product page; status dated by the DGA claim.

claims.statement: The French armament agency DGA states that it delivered the 100th Griffon of 2024 to the French Army on 16 September 2024; the GME of KNDS France, Thales and Arquus has produced the Griffon since 2018, and the LPM 2024-2030 provides for 150 Griffon in 2024 and 887 Griffon delivered by the end of 2025.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'La DGA a livré, le 16 septembre 2024, le 100e véhicule Griffon de l'année 2024 à l'armée de Terre'; produced since 2018; LPM: 150 vehicles in 2024; 887 Griffon by end of 2025.
claims.location: Paragraphs 1 and 3-4 and related news teaser
claims.uncertainty: Figures for 2024 and plan to 2025; no 2025/2026 delivery total was found.

claims.statement: Army Recognition reported that French forces landed Griffon 6x6 vehicles on 9 February 2026 in the first sea-to-land manoeuvre of exercise ORION 26 in Brittany.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'On February 9, 2026, the French Army conducted the first amphibious landing maneuvers of Griffon 6x6 armored vehicles during exercise ORION 26 in Brittany.'
claims.uncertainty: Exercise use of Griffon; secondary report.

claims.statement: Army Recognition reported that the first Belgian Griffon VBMR was presented by Mol Cy at Staden on 15 July 2025 under the Franco-Belgian CaMo programme; Janes reported in March 2026 that Belgium's Infantry School operates eight Griffon, two more are used in Tournai for training and further vehicles have been delivered to the Bataljon Bevrijding/5e Linie, which is expected to become the first fully operational Griffon battalion in the second half of 2027.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase (see evidence_items): Belgian Griffon first presented 15 Jul 2025; March 2026 deliveries to training units and the 5th Line battalion.

evidence_items.text: Army Recognition: 'On July 15, 2025, in Staden, West Flanders, the company Mol Cy officially presented this first unit' of the Griffon for the Belgian Army.

Janes (press presentation of 9 March): eight vehicles at the Infantry School in Stockem, two for training at Tournai, 'other vehicles have already been delivered' to Bataljon Bevrijding/5e Linie; first fully operational battalion expected in H2 2027; six battalions by 2030.

claims.uncertainty: The Janes article year is taken from its page date (2026-03-12); full operational capability is a stated expectation for 2027.

claims.statement: On 30 December 2025 the DGA placed an order with KNDS France, on behalf of Belgium, for 92 additional Griffon and 123 Serval; Luxembourg joins the programme through the Belgian order with 38 Jaguar and 16 Griffon.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: EDR (3 Feb 2026): 'On December 30th 2025, the DGA placed an order with KNDS France, on behalf of ... the Belgian Ministry of Defence, for 92 additional Griffon vehicles and 123 Serval vehicles'; Luxembourg: 38 Jaguar and 16 Griffon.
claims.uncertainty: Orders only; deliveries of these quantities are not reported.

claims.statement: KNDS describes the JAGUAR as an armoured reconnaissance and combat vehicle from the SCORPION programme, armed with the T40 turret (40 mm cannon) and Akeron MP anti-tank missiles, with common vetronics developed with Thales.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The JAGUAR from the SCORPION program is an Armoured Fighting Vehicle designed for reconnaissance and combat'; T40 turret and Akeron MP missile pod.
claims.uncertainty: Product page; no delivery numbers.

claims.statement: The French Ministry of the Armed Forces stated in February 2022 that the first 20 Jaguar had been delivered a few weeks earlier, with 135 Jaguar planned by the end of 2025 and a target of 300 by 2030.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'La livraison des 20 premiers Jaguar a eu lieu il y a quelques semaines ... Il est prévu la livraison de 135 Jaguar d'ici fin 2025 avec une cible de 300 d'ici à 2030.'
claims.location: Section 'Visite de la chaine d'assemblage des Jaguar'
claims.uncertainty: 2022 plan; actual 2025 totals were not found. In 2025 the army planned 33 Jaguar deliveries per FOB.

claims.statement: According to KNDS France, close to 25 Jaguar vehicles at R3 standard had been delivered to or retrofitted for the French Army as of 18 September 2026; the DGA certified the R3 standard as fit for service on 8 April 2026, the French Army authorised its operational use on 20 July 2026, and all vehicles delivered at R2 standard are to be upgraded to R3 by the end of 2027.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: Press release Versailles, 23 September 2026: first EBRC Jaguar at R3 standard delivered during summer 2026; 'close to 25' delivered or retrofitted as of 18 September 2026; R3 certified on 8 April 2026; operational use authorised 20 July 2026; R2 vehicles upgraded by end of 2027.
claims.uncertainty: Count mixes new deliveries and retrofits; total fleet size is not stated.

claims.statement: Army Recognition reported that the 1st Foreign Cavalry Regiment deployed several Jaguar to Estonia in May 2024 as part of the Lynx mission.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The 1st Foreign Cavalry Regiment (REC) had previously deployed several Jaguar vehicles to Estonia in May as part of the same Lynx mission.'
claims.uncertainty: Year is inferred from the article context (2024 archive path); secondary report.

claims.statement: The CaMo programme covers Jaguar for Belgium and Luxembourg: Luxembourg acquires 38 Jaguar through the Belgian order, and the SCORPION consortium of KNDS France, Arquus and Thales builds the Jaguar.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'With 38 Jaguar and 16 Griffon vehicles, Luxembourg acquires SCORPION vehicles' via the Belgian order; Griffon and Jaguar produced by a GME of KNDS France, Arquus and Thales.
claims.uncertainty: Order; Belgian Jaguar deliveries not found in sources read.

claims.statement: KNDS describes the SERVAL as a 4x4 light armoured vehicle designed by KNDS France and Texelis under the SCORPION programme to modernise the VAB fleet, with 31 variants and sub-variants.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The SERVAL is a 4x4 light armored vehicle, designed by KNDS France and TEXELIS as part of the SCORPION program'; chassis offers 31 variants and sub-variants.
claims.uncertainty: Product page; no delivery numbers.

claims.statement: Defence Blog reported (July 2023) that KNDS announced delivery of the 135th Serval to the French Armed Forces; the first four vehicles were delivered in May 2022; Serval vehicles are produced at Nexter's plant in Roanne.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'KNDS has announced that it has delivered the 135th Serval ... the first 4 vehicles were delivered in May 2022'; produced in Roanne.
claims.uncertainty: Secondary report of a KNDS announcement; exact announcement date not given.

claims.statement: Army Recognition reported that the French Army deployed the Serval for the first time in an external theatre (Estonia, Lynx mission) in 2024 and that the first four Serval went to CAPCIA / 51st Infantry Regiment in Mourmelon and a year later the 3rd RPIMa became the first operational unit equipped with the Serval.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'These vehicles have arrived in Estonia, marking their engagement in the Lynx mission'; '3rd Marine Infantry Parachute Regiment (RPIMa) became the first operational unit to be equipped with the Serval'.
claims.uncertainty: Article is undated in the text read; archive path indicates 2024.

claims.statement: Theatrum Belli reported that the DGA delivered the first 30 Serval Appui SCORPION to the French Army at the end of 2025 as part of a contract for 530 vehicles (more than EUR 1 billion) with deliveries until 2033; Army Recognition reported that the Ministry of the Armed Forces announced receipt of the first 30 on 21 January 2026 and that this batch is intended for operational units.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase (see evidence_items): first 30 Serval Appui delivered end 2025, announced 21 Jan 2026.

evidence_items.text: Theatrum Belli (24 Jan 2026): 'La Direction générale de l'armement a livré fin 2025 les trente premiers véhicules blindés SERVAL Appui Scorpion'; contract of 530 vehicles; deliveries until 2033.

Army Recognition: the French Army 'has officially received its first 30 Serval Appui SCORPION armored vehicles, the Ministry of the Armed Forces announced on January 21, 2026'; the batch is intended for direct integration into operational units.

claims.uncertainty: Both reports are secondary to the ministry release, which was not retrieved; the contract notification date differs between sources (31 Dec 2024 vs Feb 2025).

claims.statement: According to EDR, the 30 December 2025 DGA order for Belgium included 123 Serval, the first Serval order for the Belgian defence; the Serval vehicles are to benefit from a redesigned industrial scheme with more extensive assembly in Belgium.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: '92 additional Griffon vehicles and 123 Serval vehicles, marking the first Serval order for the benefit of the Belgian defence'; Serval assembly in Belgium to be more extensive than for Griffon.
claims.uncertainty: Order only; no Belgian Serval delivery reported.

claims.statement: KNDS describes the VBCI MK1 as in service with the French Armed Forces and as a cornerstone of mechanised units, with a 500 hp engine, a 25 mm KNDS France turret and carrying up to 11 soldiers including a crew of 3.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The VBCI MK1, in service with the French Armed Forces, is a cornerstone of mechanized units'; 500-horsepower engine; 25 mm KNDS France turret; up to 11 soldiers including crew of 3.
claims.uncertainty: Manufacturer statement without numbers or dates; the page headline is 'VBCI MK1', the MK2 is not described on it.

claims.statement: Army Technology reports that the French DGA ordered 630 VBCI in total (up to 550 infantry fighting vehicles and command post vehicles planned in two versions), that the first three production vehicles were delivered in May 2008, and that deliveries began in mid-2009.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: Order total reached 630 in September 2009; first three production vehicles delivered May 2008; 'Deliveries began in mid-2009'; 200 vehicles delivered by June 2010.
claims.uncertainty: Undated project page; the end of French production is not stated in the text read (page forecast 2015).

claims.statement: Army Recognition reported that the French Army showed a VBCI 8x8 infantry fighting vehicle with camouflage and a cage-like overhead protection structure during the live demonstration ahead of Eurosatory 2026 on 14 June 2026, retaining its 25 mm turret.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'On 14 June 2026, during the live demonstration held ahead of Eurosatory 2026, the French Army showcased its VBCI 8x8 infantry fighting vehicle'.
claims.uncertainty: Shows continued army use; not a new order or delivery.

claims.statement: EDR reported that KNDS France presented the VBCI MKII at DIMDEX 2026 as its land proposal for Qatar, described as an open weapon system able to integrate different turrets; the report describes this as an offer.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'KNDS France placed the VBCI MKII at the centre of its land proposal ... tailored to Qatar's modernisation needs'.
claims.uncertainty: Export offer / trade-fair presentation; no Qatari contract for the VBCI was found.

claims.statement: KNDS Deutschland lists GEPARD air defence systems, FENNEK reconnaissance vehicles and DINGO, MUNGO and GFF4 in its own vehicle portfolio.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: The portfolio lists GEPARD/FENNEK and protected wheeled vehicles.
claims.location: The Future of European Land Systems
claims.uncertainty: No current series production of new GEPARD vehicles is inferred from the portfolio entry.

claims.statement: KNDS describes the FENNEK family as reconnaissance vehicles with variants including engineering, anti-tank and air-defence versions, a three-person crew and a range of nearly 1,000 km.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The FENNEK family of vehicles – Specialised in the widest range of tasks'; three-man crew; range of nearly 1,000 km.
claims.uncertainty: Product page; no user list or delivery data.

claims.statement: Janes reported that on 25 July 2024 BAAINBw announced an award to KNDS Deutschland to upgrade 30 Fennek 1A2 and 50 Joint Fire Support Team (JFST) Fennek with the BAA III observation and reconnaissance set, with deliveries of the new sets scheduled for 2027-2029, and that the Fennek has been in Bundeswehr service since 2003.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'In service with the Bundeswehr since 2003, the Fennek has three crew members'; contract for BAA III sets; 'Deliveries of the new BAA IIIs, including the operational reserve, are scheduled for 2027–29.'
claims.uncertainty: Upgrade of existing vehicles; a new Fennek production lot was not found in sources read.

claims.statement: According to KNDS, it was commissioned by BAAINBw in November 2023 under a framework agreement for 50 DINGO 2 (A4 variant) protected command and special-function vehicles to replace vehicles transferred to Ukraine; KNDS states that more than 1,200 DINGO have been delivered to ten countries.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The resupply project encompasses a framework agreement for 50 DINGO 2 protected command and special-function vehicles (GFF) of the A4 variant'; 'With over 1,200 vehicles delivered to ten countries'.
claims.uncertainty: Press release is undated in the text read; Janes places the signing on 29 November 2023.

claims.statement: Janes reported that the 50 Dingo 2 A4.1 ordered by the Bundeswehr are scheduled to be delivered by the end of 2026.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The vehicles are scheduled to be delivered by the end of 2026.'
claims.uncertainty: Planned delivery date; delivery progress not reported in sources read.

claims.statement: Sicherheit & Verteidigung reported that BAAINBw signed a contract with KNDS Deutschland for a second lot of 65 Dingo 2 A4.1 on 19 December 2024 (call-off from a framework contract for up to 233 vehicles), with delivery of the first lot to be completed by end of 2026 and of the second lot from 2027 for Panzerbrigade 45 in Lithuania, and that more than 500 Dingo are in Bundeswehr use.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: second lot of 65 called off; 'Während das erste Los bis Ende 2026 ausgeliefert werden soll. Beginnt die Auslieferung des zweiten Loses ab 2027'; 'Aktuell sind mehr als 500 Dingos in unterschiedlichen Varianten in Nutzung.'
claims.uncertainty: Contract date inferred from publication on 19 Dec 2024 ('heute'); delivery dates are planned.

claims.statement: Shephard reported that KNDS Deutschland confirmed the Dingo 3 4x4 protected patrol vehicle had entered production for the German Army, with first deliveries scheduled for late 2025 from its Munich facility, following an initial order of 50 units and a second contract for 65 more.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'KNDS-Deutschland has confirmed that its latest Dingo 3 4×4 PPV has entered production for the German Army, with first deliveries scheduled to take place late in 2025'; initial order 50, second contract 65.
claims.uncertainty: Contract naming differs between sources (Dingo 2 A4.1 vs Dingo 3); first delivery was planned, not confirmed, in this report.

claims.statement: KNDS describes the DINGO 3 as the successor of the DINGO 2 HD, available as 4x4 or 6x6 platform, with more than 1,000 systems in use in seven states for the DINGO family.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'Als Nachfolger des DINGO 2 HD verfügt der DINGO 3 über leistungsgesteigerte Fähigkeiten'; 'Mit mehr als 1.000 Systemen in der Nutzung von sieben Staaten'.
claims.uncertainty: The KNDS page (1,000 systems, seven states) and the KNDS press release (1,200 vehicles, ten countries) give different family figures.

claims.statement: KNDS describes the MUNGO as an air-transportable vehicle family that can transport up to ten soldiers, from the MUNGO 2 transport version to the MUNGO N/C reconnaissance vehicle, and states that it has proven itself in many fields of military use.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The MUNGO has proven itself in many fields of military use ... it can transport up to ten fully equipped soldiers'.
claims.uncertainty: Product page; no user list, quantities or dates.

claims.statement: Shephard reported in November 2021 that a total of 455 Mungo vehicles had been procured for the German Armed Forces in various configurations and that HIL tendered maintenance for 56 Mungo ESK used by German airborne forces.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'A total of 455 Mungo vehicles have been procured for the German Armed Forces in various configurations'; tender for maintenance and repair of 56 Mungo ESK used by German airborne forces.
claims.uncertainty: Procurement total and 2021 tender; no current production, new order or 2025-2026 status was found.

claims.statement: KNDS lists the GFF 4 family of heavily armoured command and utility vehicles (up to 25 t, more than four tons payload) in its own vehicle portfolio.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The GFF 4 vehicle family from KNDS Deutschland redefines protection and flexibility ... total weight of up to 25 tons ... over four tons of payload'.
claims.uncertainty: Product page; no customer, order or delivery information.

claims.statement: Army Technology reports that BWB awarded the GFF 4 contract to KMW in 2007, that the prototype was manufactured and tested in early 2008 and handed over to the German Army in mid-2008 for reliability and mobility trials, and that about 250 vehicles are required subject to funding.
claims.evidence: Paraphrase: 'The prototype was manufactured and tested in early 2008 ... handed over to the German army in mid-2008 for reliability and mobility trials'; 'Around 250 GFF 4s are required ... orders are subject to funding permit.'
claims.uncertainty: Historic, undated project page; no series order or delivery was found in any source read.

claims.statement: WarWheels.Net reports that the Bundeswehr purchased a small number of GFF 4 for testing and evaluation purposes and that they did not appear to have been adopted at the time of writing.
claims.evidence: Excerpt: 'purchased a small number of the GFF-4's for testing and evaluation purposes, it does not seem that they were adopted at the time'.
claims.uncertainty: Enthusiast source without date (reference to 2023); not an official procurement record.

gaps.gap: No public report was found that the Bundeswehr had received its first Leopard 2 A8 by 29 Oct 2026. KNDS (Nov 2025) named April 2026 as handover start for 'the soldiers of both nations'; BAAINBw (Nov 2025) named 2027 for delivery to troops with test vehicles in 2026. Norway's first two tanks (30 Apr 2026) are the only reported handover. Absence of a report is not evidence of delay.
No source stating whether new-build Leopard 2 A7 production continues after the completion of Hungary's order (Dec 2025); Czech, Dutch and further A7 users were not documented in sources read.
Completion of the 101-vehicle A6-to-A7V modernisation batch (due 2026) and actual deliveries of Leopard 2A7A1 (Trophy) in 2025/2026 were not confirmed in sources read.

No 2025 or 2026 delivery total for Leclerc XLR (last count found: 34 delivered by 10 Dec 2024). The DGA original for the 34th delivery was not retrieved; Defense Mirror is the only source read for the count.

No public evidence of a functional RCT30 prototype test or qualification campaign by the Bundeswehr (searches: 'Boxer RCT30 Erprobung/Prototyp/trials/Eurosatory 2022'). A trade-fair presentation of the IFV mission module (2022) and a selection decision (June 2024) were found. First deliveries are planned for late 2027. Lack of a public test report is a coverage gap, not evidence of absent testing.

Delivery rate of Lot 2 beyond the first vehicle (28 Aug 2026) and the number of S1-retrofitted Lot 1 vehicles handed back to troops were not found. Bundeswehr articles on the Puma were read as raw HTML (dates 15.06.2023, 24.07.2024); no 2025/2026 Bundeswehr operational-use article was retrieved.
No 2025/2026 total for Griffon deliveries to the French Army; planning figures only (FOB: 162 Griffon planned for 2025). Belgian deliveries beyond the March 2026 snapshot not found.
Jaguar delivery totals for 2023-2026 (R2) and Belgian Jaguar deliveries were not found; only the plan (135 by end 2025) and R3 figures from Sept 2026.
The ministry's own release on the first 30 Serval Appui was not retrieved; delivery date rests on secondary reports (end 2025 vs 21 Jan 2026). Export (Belgium) deliveries not reported.

End date of French VBCI production and the current fleet count are not stated in sources read (Army Technology page undated). VBCI MKII export status (Qatar) is an offer only. The existing KNDS product page is titled VBCI MK1; a KNDS VBCI MK2 product page was not retrievable.

No current Fennek production lot or new-build order found; evidence is Bundeswehr use since 2003 and the 2024 BAA III upgrade contract (deliveries 2027-2029). Hensoldt/other user countries not documented.

Actual Dingo 2 A4.1 / Dingo 3 delivery counts were not reported in sources read; first-lot delivery is planned by end of 2026. Designation overlap (Dingo 2 A4.1 vs Dingo 3) between sources is unresolved.

No current production, new order or successor information for MUNGO (2024-2026); only a 2021 report of 455 procured vehicles was found. Searches did not find official Bundeswehr use statements for 2025/2026.

No series order, delivery or customer for GFF 4 found; only prototype trials from 2008. Wikipedia (EN) could not be retrieved (HTTP 403); a German Wikipedia/panzerbaer hint that class 4 remains open was not used as evidence. Lack of a public order is a coverage finding, not a weakness proof.
regional_presence is not part of Teilauftrag A and is not delivered in this module. Dingo/Boxer/etc. user-country lists beyond the cited sources were not compiled.
